title: Weekend deep-dive: output-hunch log — Amelia Park
content:
Purpose / quick context:
- Weekend session to capture intuition-driven observations from a small randomized sample (n=120) across hosted-prod model variants (v1.9, v2-beta). Trying to avoid confirmation bias — record hunches even if uncertain.
- Focus: hallucination modes, conditional politeness shift, token-length sensitivity, and truncation artifacts with KV cache enabled.

Sampling notes:
- Sources: production logs (anonymized), synthetic prompt bank, curated failure seeds from ENG-1428.
- Sampling strategy: stratified by token length (short < 40, mid 40-160, long >160), and by route (hosted-fast vs hosted-cost). Rough target per bucket: 40 samples.
- Annotation: quick 3-point rubric applied live (A = acceptable, B = noisy but usable, C = failure).

Quick 3-point rubric (ad-hoc):
- A (acceptable): answer is on-topic, factuality OK, formatting preserved, no obvious contradiction.
- B (noisy): answer semi-useful, minor hallucination, or odd formatting (list items merged), or truncated mid-sentence occasionally.
- C (failure): invented facts, contradictory answer, severe truncation or repeat loop.

Magic heuristics I used while scanning (notes-to-self):
- "semantic drift" if the answer begins on-topic and slides to generalities after token 80.
- "politeness flip" when a direct question produces a hedged answer only for certain system prompts.
- "kv-truncation" label when output repeats "[continued]" or ends with broken token.

Representative samples (short excerpted):
1) Prompt (short): "List three reasons remote work increases productivity."
   - v1.9 -> Output: concise list, but item 2 includes a fabricated "Zetron study 2018" (C).
   - v2-beta -> Output: list, slightly longer, hedges with "many studies" without citation (B).

2) Prompt (long, multi-step): "Draft a polite refusal email to a vendor who missed SLA, include 3 remediation asks and a suggested timeline."
   - v1.9 -> Good structure, but timeline unrealistic (asks 1-week turnaround for infra change) (B).
   - v2-beta -> Starts well, then second paragraph repeats same remediation ask with different wording, ending truncated mid-sentence (C, kv-truncation).

3) Prompt (mid): "Summarize the attached policy excerpt and highlight legal risk areas." (note: we fed an anonymized paragraph)
   - v1.9 -> Conservative summary; misses a key clause about data residency (B).
   - v2-beta -> Hallucinates a clause about GDPR Article 33 (C, invented reference).

Observed patterns / hypotheses:
- v2-beta seems more verbose and more likely to hedge; hedging correlates with fewer explicit citations but more invented references. Hypothesis: the longer decoding path increases spurious replacement tokens (model hallucinates proper nouns).
- KV cache + long sequences: higher incidence of truncation artifacts on beta. Hypothesis: cache chunking threshold may be misaligned with kernel selection; when chunk boundary hits, returns partial tokens and ends.
- Short prompts: v1.9 more likely to invent a concrete-sounding study; v2-beta prefers general hedges. Potential calibration difference in logits temperature or training data mixing.

Small quick checks to reproduce (todo):
- Re-run 10 of the C-class failures with kv_cache disabled to see if truncation persists. Link any consistent reproductions to ENG-1428.
- Vary max_new_tokens from 40->200 in increments for a failing long prompt to map threshold where truncation occurs.
- Compare sampling/top_k/top_p settings from hosted-fast vs hosted-cost (are we using different decode params?).

Immediate actionable items (for Monday):
- Create a mini-issue with 5 reproducible seeds (include full prompt + model + params + exact timestamp). Target: ENG-1428 follow-up.
- Ask infra/serving runtime for a kernel/caching trace for a failing request (include trace id).
- Add a tiny unit test to eval harness: flag when output ends in non-closed punctuation more than 20% in long bucket.

Loose notes / things I scribbled while watching samples:
- A few outputs repeat the last two tokens ("...the the"). Might be beam/decoding bug or EOS handling.
- One sample included HTML-escaped characters where original prompt had none ("&"), weird. Maybe tokenization mismatch in multi-byte sequences.
- Politeness flip sometimes coincides with presence of a system instruction (e.g., "You are a helpful assistant") vs absence. Track whether prompt template differs.

Questions I want to resolve:
- Is beta using a slightly different tokenizer or detokenization step? (check PR #983)
- Are routing policies mapping certain traffic to beta with different decode params? Need trace.
- Are quantization kernels on the Dedicated path producing different numeric stability (unlikely for hosted but worth confirming)?

Scratch TODO (short):
- [ ] Grab raw request/response pairs for top 10 C-rated samples.
- [ ] Re-run in non-streaming vs streaming; note difference.
- [ ] Drop-in simple prompt that reliably triggers invented-citation mode for v1.9; share with research for calibration.
- [ ] Add tag to eval harness: "kv-truncation" with a heuristic (endswith non-punct or token length delta > 10).

Closing thought:
- This felt like a "latent decoding instability" weekend. Not catastrophic but high signal for small upgrades: tune decode params, check kv chunk boundaries, and add preflight deterministic checks for punctuation closure on long outputs.

Notes-to-self: keep these rough — use Monday pairing session with Noelle to formalize seeds and write the mini-issue.

End of log.
